# Critique — Pattern 14 (Genetics & Family History)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Genetic Testing & Carrier Status (~10%), Family History of Disease (~60%), Reproductive Genetics, Privacy, & History Gaps (~15%), and self-monitoring fillers (~15%). No questions risked crossing into specific gene-variant territory (e.g., we avoided mentioning specific variants like BRCA1 c.5266dupC). The line between broad syndromes and implementer patterns (17+) was drawn by keeping questions strictly binary (e.g., "Have you tested positive for a known hereditary cancer syndrome?") rather than inquiring about specific locus variants or detailed haplotype sequences which belong in Layer 3 or custom implementer cards. Overlaps exist with the Cardiovascular and Metabolic domains (e.g., family history of early heart disease, thyroid disorders) because family pedigree directly impacts personal risk evaluation. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions indicating positive testing engagement, known negative status, or active health privacy management (e.g., pharmacogenomics testing, sharing results, counseling) to maintain a polarity where `1` represents unknown risk, disease presence, or history gaps. We paraphrased risk assessment frameworks like Gail and Tyrer-Cuzick. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your genetics symptoms weekly...") as genetic traits are static and do not fluctuate weekly.
